description: Nonempty text does not prove that T was written. During reparse, c reads synthetic T, then F through 🆓. The text of tt is "f", so tt receives Written and c supplies a second reading. A grammar that requires a written T observes its original token, as reparse-written-observation-head does (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a (A [+T] f)
%rule b (A [+T] [+T] f)
%rule c (A $t:tt) %conditions Written ⊆ $t.tags

%rule tt [+T 🆓] :: ($.source-text ≠ "" ⟹ Written)
%rule 🆓 [{F}]
%rule f F
